cells.A2: Apply exactly the same factual-support criteria as the first human pass.

cells.B5: Provided evidence directly or reasonably establishes the factual claim without substantive distortion.
cells.C5: An accurate paraphrase may count even if wording is different.

cells.B6: Provided evidence does not establish the factual assertion, including unwarranted extrapolations or unsupported precision.
cells.C6: A claim's real-world plausibility does not make it supported by supplied sources.

cells.B7: One or more supplied sources directly contradict the factual assertion.
cells.C7: For a binary comparison, combine with Unsupported only if this matches the experiment's binary outcome definition.

cells.B8: Insufficient interpretability or evidence to make a defensible human judgement.
cells.C8: Document frequency and exclude from binary accuracy denominators; do not force a yes/no.

cells.B9: Unsupported factual addition or inference not primarily about misreporting a specified source.
cells.C9: Keep separate from source misrepresentation when using a mutually exclusive subtype table.

cells.B10: Misreports the conclusion, direction, magnitude, population, outcome or methodological limits of a specific source.
cells.C10: Subtype assessment can overlap with unsupported status. Clearly distinguish substantive type from support label.

cells.B11: Cited source/reference does not exist or contains a fabricated bibliographic identifier under the stated verification procedure.
cells.C11: A missing citation or unsupported reference to a real document is NOT automatically a fabricated citation.

cells.B12: A valid document ID is cited but does not support the attached factual statement.
cells.C12: Record as a potential source-alignment issue; do not automatically call it a fabricated citation.

cells.B13: Compare full generated synthesis to extracted atomic claims; note factual claims the extractor omitted or incorrectly segmented.
cells.C13: This is an independent error channel; agreement on extracted claims cannot assess missed claims.

cells.B14: Do not open the separate answer key before all human claim labels and extraction notes are final.
cells.C14: Primary/secondary classifications are hidden to limit anchoring and confirmation bias.
